description: Supplier batch passport upload workflow - supplier creates batches, uploads files, sees extraction status and missing fields.

userStories.title: Prisma schema: Batch and PassportDocument models
userStories.description: As a developer, I need DB models for batches and passport documents so the workflow has persistent storage.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Batch model with fields: id, orderNumber, batchNumber, status (processing|complete|missing_information), createdAt, updatedAt
Add PassportDocument model with fields: id, batchId (FK), filename, extractedFields (Json), missingFields (String[]), createdAt
Generate and apply Prisma migration
Write a Vitest unit test that imports the Prisma client and asserts Batch and PassportDocument models exist (check prisma.batch and prisma.passportDocument are defined)
npm test passes
npm run typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Added createdAt/updatedAt to Batch, added PassportDocument model with Json fields (SQLite has no String[]). Migration 20260516133923 applied.

userStories.title: Seed data: one batch per status
userStories.description: As a developer, I need seed data covering all three statuses so the UI can be tested and demonstrated without uploads.
acceptanceCriteria: Seed creates exactly three batches: one with status processing, one complete, one missing_information
Each batch has at least one PassportDocument with mocked extractedFields (product_name, material, origin_country, supplier_name, sustainability_notes)
The missing_information batch has at least two fields in missingFields
The complete batch has all five canonical fields populated
npx prisma db seed runs without error
Write a Vitest test that runs the seed logic (or imports seed helpers) and asserts exactly three batches exist with statuses: processing, complete, missing_information
npm test passes
npm run typecheck passes
userStories.notes: seedSupplierBatches helper exported from prisma/seed-helpers.ts. 4 integration tests pass.

userStories.title: Supplier upload page: form UI
userStories.description: As a supplier, I can open an upload page and fill in order number, batch number, and attach passport files.
acceptanceCriteria: Route exists at /supplier/upload
Form has text input for order number
Form has text input for batch number
Form has file input accepting .csv, .json, .xlsx, .xml, .pdf, .txt (multiple files allowed)
Submit button is present
Page is navigable from app root or has a link from the home page
npm run typecheck passes
npm run lint passes
userStories.notes: Route at /supplier/upload. Form with orderNumber, batchNumber, multi-file input. Nav links on home page.

userStories.title: Batch creation with mock extraction
userStories.description: As a supplier, submitting the upload form creates a batch and runs mock extraction so I get results without real AI.
acceptanceCriteria: Form submission calls a server action or API route
Server action creates a Batch record with status processing initially
Mock extraction runs synchronously: randomly assigns complete or missing_information status
Creates a PassportDocument with mocked extractedFields for each uploaded file
Missing_information batches have at least one entry in missingFields
After submission, user is redirected to /supplier/batches or sees success feedback

Write Vitest unit tests for the mock extraction function: (1) returns status complete or missing_information, (2) always returns all five canonical field keys in extractedFields, (3) missing_information result has non-empty missingFields array
npm test passes
npm run typecheck passes
npm run lint passes
userStories.notes: submitBatch server action in src/app/supplier/upload/actions.ts. mockExtract in src/lib/mock-extraction.ts. Redirects to /supplier/batches.

userStories.title: Batch list with status badges
userStories.description: As a supplier, I can see all my batches and their processing status at a glance.
acceptanceCriteria: Route exists at /supplier/batches
Lists all batches ordered by createdAt descending
Each row shows: order number, batch number, status badge, created date
Status badge colors: processing=yellow, complete=green, missing_information=red
Link or button from /supplier/batches to /supplier/upload
Page works with seed data (shows three batches)
npm run typecheck passes
npm run lint passes
userStories.notes: Route at /supplier/batches. Table with order, batch, status badge (yellow/green/red), created date. Link to /supplier/upload.

userStories.title: Canonical passport fields display with missing field indicators
userStories.description: As a supplier, I can view extracted canonical fields for a batch and clearly see which fields are missing.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking a batch on /supplier/batches navigates to /supplier/batches/[id]
Detail page shows all five canonical fields: product_name, material, origin_country, supplier_name, sustainability_notes
Populated fields show their extracted value
Missing fields are visibly marked (e.g., red label, dash, or 'Missing' badge)
If status is missing_information, a summary list of missing field names is shown at the top
Page works with all three seed batches
npm run typecheck passes
npm run lint passes
userStories.notes: Route at /supplier/batches/[id]. Shows 5 canonical fields with Missing badge for nulls. Missing fields summary at top when status is missing_information.
